slides.headline: October 17, 2003: India launched its heaviest remote-sensing satellite - built to watch its own land from space.
ISRO's PSLV-C5 launched RESOURCESAT-1 from Sriharikota
slides.body: At 1,360 kg, it was India's heaviest and most advanced remote-sensing satellite at the time, placed into a polar sun-synchronous orbit roughly 817 kilometres above Earth.

slides.headline: It carried three imaging sensors built to track India's land, water and crops in far more detail than before.
slides.body: Its LISS-3, LISS-4 and AWiFS sensors extended and upgraded the data India's earlier IRS satellites had been providing - designed for a 5-year mission life, used for agriculture, water resources and land-use planning.

slides.eyebrow: Why it matters for Viksit Bharat 2047
slides.headline: A Viksit Bharat needs to see its own land clearly, on its own terms.
slides.body: A satellite built to monitor India's crops, water and land use gave planners and farmers data that didn't depend on any other country's satellite program.

sources.text: Universe Today - India launches remote sensing satellite
